Multi-asset portfolio construction and risk report

12 ETFs across equities, bonds, credit, gold and commodities  |  04 Jun 2007 to 30 Dec 2025  |  monthly rebalance, 252-day lookback, 10 bp per trade, 40% position cap  |  generated 22 Oct 2026

Data source: yfinance (adjusted closes, dividends reinvested).

From July 2008 to December 2025, the Risk Parity portfolio returned 5.4% a year at 7.8% volatility (Sharpe 0.45), against 8.8% at 12.0% for a 60/40 mix (Sharpe 0.59). Its worst drawdown was −20.4% versus −30.1%.

Portfolio construction

MethodIdeaKnown weakness
Equal WeightHold 1/N of every asset; no estimation needed.Ignores risk: equities dominate portfolio volatility.
Inverse VolatilityWeight each asset by 1/volatility.Ignores correlations between assets.
Min VarianceMinimise portfolio variance (Ledoit-Wolf covariance, 40% cap).Piles into a few low-volatility assets, mostly bonds.
Max SharpeMaximise return per unit of risk using shrunk mean estimates.Amplifies estimation error; unstable weights and high turnover.
Risk ParityEvery asset contributes equally to portfolio volatility (Spinu convex formulation).Bond-heavy; reaching equity-like returns needs leverage.
HRPCluster assets by correlation, then split risk down the tree (Lopez de Prado).Heuristic with no return view; sensitive to the clustering linkage.
60/40, SPYStatic benchmarks run through the same engine, costs and dates.Benchmarks, not strategies: 60/40 is ~90% equity risk.

Where each strategy sits against the efficient frontier

The frontier is built from full-sample means and covariance, so it is an in-sample ceiling no real strategy can reach. Strategy points use realised net returns.

Allocation through time

Capital allocation versus risk allocation

Equal capital is not equal risk. In a 60/40 mix the equity sleeve typically produces most of the volatility, which is the central argument for risk-based construction.

Is the VaR model any good? Out-of-sample backtest at 99%

Each day's VaR uses only the previous 250 days. A well-calibrated 99% model is breached about 1% of the time; the Kupiec test rejects models whose exception rate differs from that by more than chance. Basel zones apply the regulatory traffic-light rule to the most recent 250 days.

Cleaning policy: forward-fill gaps of at most 3 days, never back-fill, drop assets with more than 5% missing, flag but never silently delete extreme moves. 0 flagged observations and 0 corrective actions are logged in data_audit_log.csv.

Method and limits

  • No look-ahead. Signals use a trailing 252-day window ending at the signal close; trades execute 1 day later. Parameters are fixed defaults and were not tuned on the results shown.
  • Estimation error is the main enemy. Covariances use Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage; max-Sharpe means are shrunk toward the cross-sectional average; positions are capped at 40%.
  • Costs. A flat 10 bp per unit of traded notional. No bid-ask spread model, market impact, taxes or financing; long-only, unlevered.
  • Universe. A fixed list of liquid ETFs chosen with hindsight, and only assets with history over the full window. This carries survivorship and selection bias.
  • Frontier and stress shocks. The frontier is in-sample by construction. Hypothetical shocks are round-number assumptions.
  • Statistical power. 19 years is a handful of independent market regimes. Differences in Sharpe between neighbouring strategies are usually within sampling error (see the intervals above).
